selection.justification: Silicon is an inorganic semiconductor that is extremely well-represented in the Materials Project dataset. MACE-MP-0 is trained on ~150k inorganic materials including many silicon-containing structures (elemental Si, silicates, silicon oxides, etc.). The diamond-cubic structure of silicon is a fundamental crystal structure that will be in the training set. This model provides state-of-the-art accuracy for geometry optimization of inorganic crystals and will reliably predict the lattice constant to within ~1% of DFT/experimental values. It supports stress tensor prediction which is essential for cell relaxation.
selection.cautions: None significant for this use case. Silicon in diamond-cubic structure is a textbook example well within the model's domain. The mace-mp-0b variant could also work if faster inference is needed, though for a single bulk relaxation the speed difference is negligible and the higher accuracy of mace-mp-0 is preferred.

research_goal: Relax bulk silicon in the diamond-cubic structure to its equilibrium geometry — optimize both the cell and the ionic positions — and report the optimized cubic lattice constant.
notes: MACE mace-mp-0 (medium, inorganic). LAMMPS-capable via pair_style mliap unified.
